conventions.convention: Use c = ℏ = 1, global gauge group SU(2), and dimensionless positive gauge coupling g. The classical model does not supply a constructed quantum SCFT.
Radial adjoints satisfy Pμ† = Kμ, D† = D, S = Q†, and δ = 2{S,Q} = E − 2J1 − 3R/2. The conjugate scalar-primary anticommutator has the opposite R sign.

Index blocks combine both parities at fixed joint energy and charge. Reducing projections preserve actual operator domains; the weighted exponential must be bounded trace class. Total gap multiplicities and the protected kernel may be infinite.
The selected N=1 R symmetry assigns scalar charge 2/3 to each adjoint chiral superfield. Positive-branch shortening means annihilation by the selected Q.

For the specified closed oriented Riemannian four-manifold and defining SU(2) trace, B = −tr₂ and k = −⟨c₂(E),[X]⟩. Full AC is assumed for the characteristic-class comparison. Self-dual action factors are q^k; anti-self-dual factors are conjugate(q)^kA with kA = −k.

Center charges lie in Z₂ × Z₂ with pairing em′ − me′ modulo 2. S(e,m) = (m,−e) and T(e,m) = (e+m,m); these may change the global form. Their physical duality interpretation is source-reported, not proved.

The quadratic-composite example assumes a nonzero scalar superconformal primary, an exact R-symmetry-preserving renormalization prescription, and Q annihilation; engineering dimension alone is not used to establish scaling dimension.

load_bearing.statement: Defines conditional graded Hilbert-space superconformal representation data, radial adjoints and the selected scalar-primary anticommutators, reducing-block and trace-class index hypotheses, and source-qualified SU(2) coupling and center-charge conventions. It asserts neither a continuum SCFT construction nor quantum S-duality equivalence.

In a positive Hilbert-space representation of the selected N=1 superconformal subalgebra with the stated common invariant domain and radial adjoints, a nonzero scalar superconformal primary satisfies d ≥ 3|r|/2. For r ≥ 0 equality holds exactly when Q annihilates the primary; for r ≤ 0 it holds exactly when the conjugate supercharge annihilates it.

Under the Statement's closed odd adjoint-supercharge, composition-domain, kernel-domain, self-adjoint DQ, countable finite reducing graded-block, block-nilpotency, maximal direct-sum-domain, diagonal nonnegative δ, even blockwise commuting insertion, and trace-class heat-weighted insertion hypotheses, Tr((-1)^F exp(−βδ)U) = Tr_kerδ((-1)^F U) for every β > 0, and ker δ = ker Q ∩ ker S. The trace is independent of β; continuous-spectrum and non-trace-class formal path integrals are excluded.

concerns.concern: The line-operator paragraph says a Wilson line is 'parallel transport traced in a representation' and a ’t Hooft line is 'specified by a magnetic singularity around the support curve'. It supplies neither a specified curve and closed-loop/end-point convention for the traced transport nor mathematical magnetic-singularity data, and identifies no exact earlier definition supplying them. The finite center-charge arithmetic is complete, but these physical operator descriptions fall short of the required explicit definitions.

The Kapustin–Witten source locator and Definition references identify §4.2 for the Euclidean theta term on printed pp. 47–48. In the cited version, equation (4.16), giving that term, is on p. 47 within §4.1; §4.2 begins on p. 49. Checked against [Kapustin–Witten](https://arxiv.org/pdf/hep-th/0604151v3). The local sign calculation is unaffected.

seams_checked.note: Checked both page inventories and the relevant vacuum/Coulomb-branch definitions. This is a reading prerequisite; the assigned items do not import Seiberg–Witten effective data as SCFT or S-duality proofs, or identify its formal charge lattice with the center-charge line spectrum.

Checked the Wilsonian action definition against the protected-data coupling paragraph. The consumer explicitly distinguishes physical τ from the earlier formal Wilsonian coupling coordinate and does not infer continuum existence or deformation invariance from perturbative nonrenormalization.

The opened N=4 postulate supplies the global SU(2) group, classical field content, natural units, and normalization. The consumer preserves its adopted-invariance and no-quantum-construction qualifications.

The quadratic-primary example uses the postulate's adjoint field and canonical rescaling by g. Quantum primary existence, symmetry-preserving renormalization, and shortening remain explicit additional assumptions; the classical postulate is not cited as establishing them.
